title: [research] Expert-only ternary: multi-block residual / output fidelity (follow-on to #64 / RM-249)
description:
**Agent:** SuperGrok Heavy multi-agent (Grok 4.5 · Chaos Goblin · Cosmic Trickster · Mad Scientist)
**Follow-on to:** PR [rmems/grok-ozempic#64](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-genuine-grok-1-block-0-forward-route-preservation-measurement-61-e98adb2f79c9) / issue [#61](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-249/experiment-implement-genuine-grok-1-block-0-forward-and-measure-post) / Linear [RM-249](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-249)

**Post-v0.2.0 research path** — may couple with GOZ1 container version bump once [#65](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-251/bug-goz1-persists-no-per-tensor-ternary-scale-so-a-pack-cannot-be) lands

## Core question

> What happens to **block-output fidelity** and the **residual stream** when experts are ternary across **multiple blocks**?

PR [rmems/grok-ozempic#64](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-genuine-grok-1-block-0-forward-route-preservation-measurement-61-e98adb2f79c9) closed the *routing* question for block 0 under expert-only ternary:

| Metric (block 0, expert-only ternary) | Observed |
| -- | -- |
| Router top-1 / top-2 agreement | **1.000000** |
| Block-output cosine | **\~0.964** |
| Attention-ternary top-1 (contrast) | ~0.551 |

Routing is structurally preserved when routers stay high-precision and only experts (slots 00–02, ~98.21% of parameters) are ternary. **Cross-block residual accumulation and output fidelity are still unmeasured.**

Block-0 expert-only ternary already sits below the historical 0.995 cosine gate. We do not yet know whether that ~0.036 gap compounds, saturates, or self-corrects across blocks.

## Why this is next

* [rmems/grok-ozempic#64](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-genuine-grok-1-block-0-forward-route-preservation-measurement-61-e98adb2f79c9) answered single-block route preservation with a genuine forward, not a proxy.
* [#59](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-245/finish-run3-pilot-matrix-blocks-8286063-expert-only-mode) is still the *old proxy matrix* on blocks 8/28/60/63 — it does not run full residual-stream fidelity under expert-only ternary.
* The asymmetric tier policy (experts ternary, attention higher-precision, routers/norms preserved) is only scientifically justified for multi-block if residual drift stays bounded.
* This decides whether the 98% expert-ternary memory win (~576 GiB FP16 experts → ~72–77 GiB GOZ1) is viable beyond a single block.

## Scope

### Required

* Experts only ternary (GOZ1); attention, routers, and norms preserved at higher precision
* Real residual stream path (not embedding-only proxy)
* At least a short multi-block set: block 0 + one mid + one late **or** a short sequential chain (0 → 1 → …)
* Same provenance discipline as [rmems/grok-ozempic#64](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-genuine-grok-1-block-0-forward-route-preservation-measurement-61-e98adb2f79c9) (checkpoint, pack, τ, commit, token rows)

### Measurements (per block / accumulated)

* Block-output cosine vs FP reference
* Residual-stream cosine / residual drift norm
* Router top-1 / top-2 set agreement (expect near 1.0 if policy holds)
* Expert-load JS divergence + max per-expert load-share delta
* Optional: stratified by original router margin

### Decision output (one of)

1. Expert-only ternary remains viable for multi-block (drift bounded / non-compounding)
2. Needs a correction mechanism (e.g. residual feedback, scale refresh, occasional higher-precision expert block)
3. Expert tier needs higher precision than single-scale ternary for multi-block
4. Inconclusive — name the unresolved architectural / activation-supply gap

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Expert-only ternary multi-block (or short chain) harness runs on real Grok-1 weights
- [ ] Residual and block-output metrics reported with full provenance
- [ ] Router agreement remains near 1.0 under the preserved-router policy (or failure is explained)
- [ ] Results under `reports/` (Markdown + machine-readable JSON)
- [ ] Bounded decision output as above
- [ ] No router/norm/attention ternaryization in the primary arm

title: [bug] GOZ1 persists no per-tensor ternary scale, so a pack cannot be dequantized from its own contents
description:
**Agent:** Claude Code: Fable 5 (xhigh)

Found while implementing the genuine block-0 forward for [#61](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-249/experiment-implement-genuine-grok-1-block-0-forward-and-measure-post) (PR [rmems/grok-ozempic#64](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-genuine-grok-1-block-0-forward-route-preservation-measurement-61-e98adb2f79c9)).

## Problem

`quantize_f32` (`src/core/quantizer.rs`) computes both a per-tensor `rms` and the derived firing threshold `τ`, and returns them on `QuantizedTensor`:

```rust
pub rms: f32,
pub threshold: f32,
```

The GOZ1 container then **discards both**. A ternary tensor header carries only:

```
name, shape, tensor_type (0=f16, 1=ternary), data_offset
```

and the payload is 2 bits per trit and nothing else. There is no per-tensor scale anywhere in the header or in the `oz.*` metadata.

**Consequence: a GOZ1 pack cannot be dequantized from its own contents.** Trits alone give you `{-1, 0, +1}` with no magnitude, so `w ≈ α · t` has no recoverable `α`. Any consumer — `MyelinBackend`, a CUDA GEMV kernel, or a host-side check — needs a scale that the format does not carry.

## Why it matters now

Every route-preservation figure in [rmems/grok-ozempic#64](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-genuine-grok-1-block-0-forward-route-preservation-measurement-61-e98adb2f79c9) had to reconstruct with an **oracle** scale derived from the original f32 weights:

```
α* = Σ|w| over fired trits / count(fired)
```

That is the least-squares optimal single scale for the pack's own trit pattern, so it is the *best* any runtime could do — which conveniently makes [rmems/grok-ozempic#64](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-genuine-grok-1-block-0-forward-route-preservation-measurement-61-e98adb2f79c9)'s numbers a clean lower bound on damage. But it also means those numbers are **not reproducible from the pack alone**, and a real runtime has no way to obtain that α. The measurement harness works around a format gap rather than exercising a real inference path.

This becomes blocking the moment anything consumes a pack without the original checkpoint alongside it.

## Suggested fix

Persist the scale per ternary tensor in the tensor header. `quantize_f32` already has the value, so this is a format/writer change, not new math.

Worth deciding explicitly:

1. **Which scale to store.** `rms`/`threshold` are what the quantizer already computes, but the *reconstruction*-optimal value is `α* = Σ|w|(fired)/count(fired)`, which is not the same number. Storing α* is the one that minimizes reconstruction error; storing `rms` preserves the ability to re-derive τ. Storing both is 8 bytes per tensor.
2. **Granularity.** Per-tensor matches how `quantize_f32` works today. Per-output-channel was measured in [rmems/grok-ozempic#52](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/research-embedding-t-sweeps-for-spiking-sparse-goz1-51-rm-201-3e12e6a9b503)/[rmems/grok-ozempic#57](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-int8-dequant-export-bounded-block-0-goz1-pilot-53-rm-222-03ffe2525928) at ≈0.896 cosine vs ≈0.887 per-tensor — a real but small gain, and a much larger header. Per-tensor is probably right for now; the field should not preclude a later per-channel variant.
3. **Version bump.** Adding a header field changes the container. `oz.quantization_version` is currently `1`; this likely wants `2` with a documented reader fallback, since packs already exist on disk.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Ternary tensor headers carry a scale (documented: which quantity, what granularity)
- [ ] `--verify` checks the scale is present and finite for every ternary tensor
- [ ] A pack can be dequantized with no access to the source weights
- [ ] Container version bumped with a documented policy for existing v1 packs
- [ ] Consumer scripts prefer the stored scale and fall back to the oracle α only for legacy v1 packs, with the fallback recorded in report provenance
- [ ] Round-trip test: quantize → write → read → reconstruct matches the in-memory reconstruction

## Non-goals

* Per-channel or grouped scales (separate decision; see 2 above)
* Changing the GIF threshold formula
* CUDA/Myelin kernel work

| PR [rmems/grok-ozempic#64](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-genuine-grok-1-block-0-forward-route-preservation-measurement-61-e98adb2f79c9) / [#61](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-249/experiment-implement-genuine-grok-1-block-0-forward-and-measure-post) / [RM-249](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-249/experiment-implement-genuine-grok-1-block-0-forward-and-measure-post) | **Discovered during** — oracle α workaround used for all block-0 figures |

title: [experiment] Implement genuine Grok-1 block-0 forward and measure post-attention route preservation
description:
## Objective

Replace PR [rmems/grok-ozempic#57](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-int8-dequant-export-bounded-block-0-goz1-pilot-53-rm-222-03ffe2525928)'s single-projection routing proxy with a bounded, genuine
Grok-1 block-0 forward measurement using real checkpoint weights and real token
embedding rows.

The experiment must reconstruct the actual path from block-0 input through:

1. pre-attention RMSNorm
2. grouped-query attention projections
3. attention output projection
4. residual addition
5. post-attention / MoE-input RMSNorm
6. the preserved FP16/BF16 MoE router

Compare the original dequantized block path against the GOZ1 ternary-attention
path while keeping routers and norms preserved.

## Why this is next

PR [rmems/grok-ozempic#57](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-int8-dequant-export-bounded-block-0-goz1-pilot-53-rm-222-03ffe2525928) established useful but proxy-relative evidence:

* real token-embedding rows differ materially from Gaussian random inputs
* projection-output cosine does not guarantee routing agreement
* single-scale ternary attention causes substantial direct-path routing drift
* router FP16 round-trip is not the primary source of the observed drift

However, PR [rmems/grok-ozempic#57](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-int8-dequant-export-bounded-block-0-goz1-pilot-53-rm-222-03ffe2525928) does not execute the actual transformer block. Its routing proxy
computes one attention projection and feeds that result to the router. The real
router consumes the normalized residual stream after attention.

Until the genuine block path is evaluated, the current top-1/top-2 agreement,
load-JS, residual-inclusive estimates, and norm-order sweeps are not sufficient
to decide whether attention must leave the ternary tier.

## Scope

### Required

* Block 0 only
* Real Grok-1 checkpoint weights
* Real token-embedding rows sampled deterministically
* Correct grouped-query attention dimensions:
  * 48 query heads
  * 8 key/value heads
  * head dimension 128
* Resolve the four block-normalization tensors to their actual architectural
  roles from authoritative Grok-1 code/checkpoint structure
* Identify Q, K, V, and output projection slots explicitly
* Implement the actual attention calculation required for block 0
* Preserve router and normalization tensors
* Compare reference attention weights against packed GOZ1 ternary attention
  weights
* Record complete provenance for token selection, tensor-role mapping, checkpoint,
  pack, thresholds, and implementation commit

### Measurements

For both reference and quantized paths, record:

* attention-output cosine
* residual-stream cosine before MoE normalization
* normalized MoE-input cosine
* router-logit cosine
* router top-1 agreement
* router top-2 set agreement
* expert-load distribution
* expert-load JS divergence
* maximum per-expert load-share delta
* residual drift norm
* per-token router margin before and after quantization

Also stratify route flips by original router margin so we can distinguish:

* unavoidable flips on nearly tied experts
* damaging flips on high-confidence routes

## Required baselines

Run at least:

1. FP32/dequantized reference
2. FP16 round-trip control with no ternary attention
3. Current GOZ1 attention τ = 0.4
4. Best routing-oriented τ found by PR [rmems/grok-ozempic#57](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-int8-dequant-export-bounded-block-0-goz1-pilot-53-rm-222-03ffe2525928)
5. Optional higher-precision or correction baseline if straightforward

The FP16 control must demonstrate that the measurement implementation itself
does not create meaningful route drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Architectural tensor roles are resolved and documented with evidence
- [ ] Genuine block-0 attention + residual + MoE-input norm executes
- [ ] Reference and GOZ1 paths use identical token rows and preserved router/norms
- [ ] FP16 control produces near-identical routing
- [ ] Route metrics are measured from the actual router input, not a projection proxy
- [ ] Results are written under `reports/grok-1-full-block-forward/`
- [ ] Machine-readable JSON and readable Markdown report are produced
- [ ] Tests cover tensor-role validation, GQA shapes, masking, residual wiring,
      norm placement, and route metrics
- [ ] No full-model inference and no blocks beyond block 0

## Decision output

The report must end with one of these bounded conclusions:

1. current ternary attention is viable for further block-matrix testing
2. ternary attention needs a correction mechanism
3. attention should move to a higher-precision tier
4. result remains inconclusive because an explicitly named architectural element
   could not be resolved

Do not relax the route-preservation gates merely to obtain a passing result.

## Non-goals

* Full 64-block model
* Full-model text generation
* Blocks 8/28/60/63
* CUDA optimization
* Myelin integration
* Quantizing routers or norms
* New SAAQ formula
* Repeating the full [#59](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-245/finish-run3-pilot-matrix-blocks-8286063-expert-only-mode) proxy matrix

title: [grok-ozempic] Research: activity-aware / tier-aware τ for spiking-sparse GOZ1
description:
> **Linear SoT:** [RM-201](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-201/grok-ozempic-research-activity-aware-tier-aware-t-for-spiking-sparse)
>
> Body synced from Linear. Prefer Linear for status; this GH issue is the GitHub twin.

## Context

[RM-190](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-190) / [GH#39](<https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/issues/39>) produced the first real GOZ1 from `embedding.slot_00.token_embedding`:

* τ = 0.05 × RMS → **\~4.17% zeros**, ~96% ±1 (**dense / sign-like**)
* Not sparse SNN activity; quantizer behaved correctly
* Result is weight distribution vs default τ, not CPU vs GPU

Algorithm (`src/core/quantizer.rs`):

```text
rms = sqrt(mean(w²))
τ   = gif_threshold × rms
|w| < τ → 0;  w ≥ τ → +1;  w ≤ −τ → −1
```

Default `gif_threshold = 0.05` (`types.rs`). Precedence (`precision.rs`): per-tensor ternary_candidate → manifest defaults → CLI config.

**Trap for sweeps:** stock `baseline.json` bakes `defaults.gif_threshold: 0.05`, so CLI `--gif-threshold` is **ignored** for actual quantize τ. Use a temp manifest without defaults.gif_threshold, or bake τ into defaults per run.

BitNet b1.58 uses absmean + RoundClip (different scale story). GOZ1 is PTQ saliency gate — same alphabet, different control knob.

This issue tracks the **science** so we can *choose* event-driven / spiking-sparse ternary.

## Goal

Make ternary packing policy **activity-aware / tier-aware** so embeddings, MoE experts, and attention land on different sparsity regimes. **Success = measured non-trivial zeros under GIF, not dense-sign packs.**

## Work (research, not kernel work)

- [ ] τ sweeps on embedding (0.0 control, 0.05 default, 0.1 → 0.2 → 0.5 …) with trit histograms / sparsity
- [ ] Same on ≥1 expert projection and ≥1 attention tensor (needs multi-tensor export)
- [ ] Define per-tier defaults (embedding vs MoE vs attn; router = preserve)
- [ ] Document when dense sign-like is OK vs when sparsity is required
- [ ] Optional: per-row / per-group RMS or absmean arm
- [ ] Feed findings into SAAQ 1.5 multi-tensor policy notes
- [ ] Land reports under `reports/grok-1-first-embed-goz1/` (or similar) with commands

### CLI sketch (embedding isolate)

```bash
# STAGE = sole embedding npy dir
# MANI = JSON without defaults.gif_threshold (CLI controls τ)
for TAU in 0.0 0.05 0.1 0.2 0.5; do
  cargo run --release --features cli -- quantize-goz1 \
    --input-dir "$STAGE" --output "goz1-tau-${TAU}.goz1" \
    --manifest "$MANI" --gif-threshold "$TAU" --verify
done
```

## Non-goals

* No CUDA / myelin kernel work (→ [LIM-890](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/LIM-890) / [RM-199](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-199))
* No fake sparsity in the packer — zeros from threshold policy only
* No full-model requant or quality claims
* No brainstem-daemon / runtime integration
* No router ternary

## Acceptance

* Written comparison of sparsity vs τ for ≥2 tensor families (embedding + one other when exportable)
* Recommended default τ (or policy) per tier for next multi-tensor run
* Clear statement of when GOZ1 ternary is event-driven vs dense
* Document baseline-manifest CLI τ trap

description:

>
> Body synced from Linear. Prefer Linear for status; this GH issue is the GitHub twin.

## Verdict (Grok Build multi-agent research)

**HYBRID — KEEP SAAQ 1.5 as runtime default.** Do **not** mint SAAQ 2.0 from SymbolicRegression on existing latent CSVs.

| Option | Decision |
| -- | -- |
| KEEP 1.5 | **Yes** — default formula + campaign label |
| PATCH 1.5 | Only for measured defects (cold-start/silence), not prettier SR trees |
| NEW formula (2.0) | **Not yet** — only after an **external** `y` exists |
| HYBRID | Freeze 1.5 hot path; SR = research against external objectives |

**Confidence:** ~0.86

---

## Two meanings of "SAAQ 1.5" (do not conflate)

### A. Formula version — `SaaqV1_5SqrtRate`

```text
saaq_delta_q_target = 0.0573 * sqrt(max(avg_pop_firing_rate_hz, 0.0))
                    + 0.496  * saaq_delta_q_prev
```

* Eng: `corinth-canal/src/latent.rs`, `SAAQ-latent`
* Doc: `corinth-canal/docs/SAAQ_FORMULA_COMPARISON.md`
* Provenance HoF: `Surrogate_Viz.jl/outputs/20260416_232439_RN5oWH/hall_of_fame.csv`

### B. Engineering epic / campaign

Multi-model RE4 lineup, dual calibrator, validation dashboards — product line **around** the formula.

### C. grok-ozempic "SAAQ" (third layer)

GOZ1 ternary packing: `τ = gif_threshold × rms(layer)` (default 0.05). **Not** the latent AR(1) law.

Linear "SAAQ 1.5 multi-tensor GOZ1" ≠ Surrogate_Viz "sqrt-rate formula."

---

## Why 1.5 is good enough *as default ΔQ*

* Simple, hot-path cheap (rate + AR only)
* Dual calibrator + CSV contract already A/B both rules
* Ecosystem frozen: SAAQ-latent tests, MoE campaigns, magere `saaq_v1_5`
* Default in docs (`SAAQ_RULE=saaq_v1_5`)

## Why not create a new formula in Surrogate_Viz *right now*

1. **Circular SR:** targeting `saaq_delta_q_target` rediscovers exact 1.5 — fidelity, not a better law
2. Raw discovery rediscovers synthetic power/400 targets — different problem class
3. **No closed loop into quant:** packing still uses static `gif_threshold`
4. Paired validation often null under some conditions
5. Spikenaut is mining/GPU/HFT telemetry — good for **external** y, not latent SAAQ schema

---

## What a real new Surrogate_Viz formula would need

**Forbidden y for promotion:** `y = saaq_delta_q_target` (circular)

**Allowed external y:** thermal/power, GOZ1 sparsity+quality under τ(ΔQ), router health as features only, closed-loop Δτ

- [ ] Doc split: formula vs campaign vs GOZ1 gif_threshold
- [ ] Freeze default `SaaqV1_5SqrtRate`; dual emit both rules
- [ ] Ban circular SR for promotion
- [ ] Spec external primary y + success thresholds
- [ ] Optional closed-loop spike: ΔQ → τ on one embedding GOZ1
- [ ] If PATCH: cold-start/silence only + unit tests
- [ ] If 2.0 later: new enum + dual columns; Surrogate_Viz mode targeting external y

## Non-goals

* Do not block GOZ1 / spiking-sparse τ / myelin work
* Do not auto-edit 0.0573/0.496 from a single Spikenaut or MoE Pareto row

## Acceptance

- [ ] Explicit statement that Linear SAAQ 1.5 GOZ1 epic ≠ formula rediscovery
- [ ] External-y experiment design ready before any SAAQ 2.0 issue

## Context

* Path: `/home/raulmc/.models/xai-grok-1/ckpt-0`
* **770** shards, ~297 GiB
* First-target shard: `tensor00000_000` (~3.1 GiB) = f32 `(131072, 6144)` token embedding

`xai-dissect` already reads pickle natively; reuse its loaders or a one-off Python script rather than inventing a second parser in-repo if possible.

## Repo / surfaces

| Surface | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `/home/raulmc/.models/xai-grok-1/ckpt-0/tensor00000_000` | Source pickle embedding |

| Suggested export root | e.g. `/home/raulmc/.models/xai-grok-1/export-npy/` or `/tmp/grok1-embed-npy/` |

## Implementation plan

1. Prefer **embedding-only** export first (not full 770) to save time/disk for the first experiment.
2. Choose format:
   * **Recommended for first target:** single flat `.npy` named so the stream scanner finds it (document exact filename convention stream expects), **or** one small safetensors file with a tensor key matching the manifest rule you will use.
3. Extract f32 payload from pickle `tensor00000_000` → shape `(131072, 6144)`.
4. Write converter script/command under repo `scripts/` or document one-liner if external tool is enough.
5. Smoke-load with a tiny Rust test or `run_quantization` dry path once CLI exists; until then, verify with Python/`numpy.load` + shape/dtype assert.
6. Document output path in a short comment on GH#37 for [RM-190](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-190/grok-ozempic-gh39-quantize-token-embedding-goz1) consumers.
7. Optional follow-up: full 770-tensor export (disk-heavy; out of first-experiment critical path).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At least the embedding tensor exists on disk as safetensors or `.npy` with dtype f32 and shape `(131072, 6144)`
- [ ] File(s) are discoverable by `stream` scanners (`*.safetensors` or `.npy` dir layout)
- [ ] Conversion command/script is documented (README snippet or `scripts/` + GH comment)

## Validation

ls -lh /home/raulmc/.models/xai-grok-1/ckpt-0/tensor00000_000
# After export (example for npy):
python3 - <<'PY'

assert a.dtype == np.float32 and a.shape == (131072, 6144), (a.dtype, a.shape)

* Inference quality

title: Add unified check, test, bench, and build commands for agent verification
description:
**Agent:** Grok Build: Grok 4.5 (xAI) · **Issue:** [RM-250](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-250/add-unified-check-test-bench-and-build-commands-for-agent-verification) / Linear [RM-250](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-250/add-unified-check-test-bench-and-build-commands-for-agent-verification)

## Objective

Create a small, documented, reproducible command surface that lets humans and coding agents detect repository failures before opening or updating a PR.

An agent should not need to inspect every workflow, Cargo feature, Python test directory, or local checkpoint convention to determine whether its change is safe.

## Problem

The repository currently has several separate validation paths:

* Rust formatting, linting, tests, and feature builds
* Python script unit tests
* shell-script syntax checks
* workflow/config validation
* lightweight local tests
* large-checkpoint experiments
* optional CUDA / RTX 5080 checks
* benchmarks

These checks differ in runtime, hardware requirements, required data, and environment variables. Agents can therefore:

* run only a partial test suite
* omit required Cargo features
* confuse missing local data with a code failure
* report success without running the relevant experiment checks
* waste time discovering commands already encoded elsewhere
* introduce benchmark regressions without a stable comparison command

Today the knowledge is scattered across:

| Surface | Location |
| -- | -- |
| CI Rust matrix | `.github/workflows/rust.yml` |
| CI Python unit tests | `.github/workflows/python-scripts.yml` |
| Docker image build | `.github/workflows/docker.yml` |
| Agent fast path | `.claude/commands/smoke.md` |
| Agent full ship checklist | `.claude/commands/pr-ready.md` |
| Session rules | `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/agent-workflow.md` |
| Block pilot experiment | `scripts/block_pilot_goz1.sh` |
| τ-sweep experiment | `scripts/tau_sweep_embedding.sh` |

There is **no root** `justfile` (or equivalent single entry point) yet. `just` is available on the primary dev machine (`just 1.55.1`).

## Goal

Provide one clear developer interface with named verification tiers:

```bash
just check              # fast static gates (iterate)
just test               # unit + integration tests (no multi-GiB weights)
just build              # compile matrix matching CI build step
just bench              # stable comparison entry (see tier notes)
just ci                 # local pre-PR parity with CI (no Docker unless requested)
just experiment-smoke   # optional local data path; clear skip vs fail
just doctor             # env / data / tool diagnosis (never confuses missing data with code bugs)
```

Default recipe lists all tiers: `just` / `just --list`.

## Proposed tiers (implementation contract)

Prefer a root `justfile` that shells out to the same Cargo/Python/bash commands already used in CI and agent docs. Prefer `--locked` for local recipes even when CI is slightly looser (matches `CLAUDE.md` / `/pr-ready`).

| Recipe | Intent | Runtime / hardware | Must include | Must not |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `check` | Fast static quality while editing | CPU, seconds–1 min | `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo clippy --all-targets --features cli --locked -- -D warnings` | Full all-features matrix; Docker; checkpoints |
| `test` | Correctness without large weights | CPU, a few minutes | `cargo test --features cli --locked`; all `python3 -m unittest scripts.test_*` modules that CI runs | Real ckpt-0 pickle / multi-GiB packs; CUDA |
| `build` | Compile all targets | CPU | `cargo build --all-targets --all-features --locked` | Tests |
| `bench` | Stable performance entry point | CPU (GPU optional later) | Documented, repeatable command; if no `[[bench]]` yet: release micro-path or explicit “no harness — exit non-zero with message” policy (choose one in PR and stick to it). Do **not** silently succeed with empty output | Require multi-GiB checkpoints; invent kernel benches (those belong in `myelin-accelerator`) |
| `ci` | Local “will CI pass?” | CPU, slower | Match `.github/workflows/rust.yml` spirit + Python suite from `python-scripts.yml`: fmt, clippy **all-features** `-D warnings`, test **all-targets --all-features**, build all-features, `cargo doc --no-deps --all-features`, Python unittests, `bash -n` on `scripts/*.sh`. Optional: `actionlint` / `shellcheck` if installed (skip with note if missing — do not fail `ci` solely for optional tools) | Docker image builds (slow; path-scoped in `/pr-ready`); CUDA; real quant experiments |
| `experiment-smoke` | Prove experiment scripts still wire | May need local data | Prefer **no-weight** smoke first: release CLI build + `quantize-goz1 --help` / `validate-ingest --help`; then, only if doctor paths exist, a **bounded** optional step (e.g. dry-run SAAQ or documented pilot dry path). Missing data → **exit non-zero with explicit “missing data / set CKPT or GROK_OZEMPIC_DISSECT_RUN”** (not a silent pass) | Claim full pilot certification; mutate `dissect/` |
| `doctor` | Diagnose environment | Instant | Print versions (`rustc`, `cargo`, `just`, `python3`, numpy if present); feature/CLI binary status; presence of key paths (`$HOME/.models/xai-grok-1/ckpt-0`, `GROK_OZEMPIC_DISSECT_RUN` / default xai-dissect run3 root, in-tree manifests); optional GPU/CUDA.jl probe status. Exit 0 when report completes; use structured ok/warn/missing lines so agents can parse | Run long tests or packs |

### Composition rules

* Recipes should be **composable** (`ci` may call `check`/`test`/`build` pieces, or duplicate commands for clearer CI logs — either is fine if documented).
* Fail **fast** on first hard error.
* Prefer **print the command** before running it (agents need evidence).
* No secrets, no multi-GiB artifacts under the repo.

## Mapping to existing sources of truth

| Existing | Maps into |
| -- | -- |
| `/smoke` (fmt + clippy cli + test cli) | `just check` + `just test` |
| `/pr-ready` quality gates | `just ci` |
| `rust.yml` | core of `just ci` |
| `python-scripts.yml` | `just test` / `just ci` Python steps |
| `block_pilot_goz1.sh` / `tau_sweep_embedding.sh` | `just experiment-smoke` optional path + `just doctor` path checks |
| Kernel CUDA benches | **Out of scope** here (`kernel-boundary` → `myelin-accelerator`) |

## Documentation deliverables

1. Root `justfile` with recipes above and short comments.
2. **README.md** — short “Developer verification” section pointing at `just --list` and the tier table.
3. `CLAUDE.md` **/** `AGENTS.md` **/** `.claude/rules/agent-workflow.md` — quality-gate section prefers `just check` / `just ci` over ad-hoc cargo lines (keep cargo lines as equivalent fallback).
4. `.claude/commands/smoke.md` **and** `pr-ready.md` — call `just` recipes so agents do not diverge from humans.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Root `justfile` exists; `just --list` shows at least: `check`, `test`, `build`, `bench`, `ci`, `experiment-smoke`, `doctor`.
- [ ] `just check` fails on fmt or clippy (cli features) warnings.
- [ ] `just test` runs Rust CLI-feature tests **and** the same Python unittest modules as `python-scripts.yml`.
- [ ] `just build` builds `--all-targets --all-features --locked`.
- [ ] `just ci` covers the Rust workflow steps + Python unittests + `bash -n scripts/*.sh`.
- [ ] `just doctor` reports tool versions and checkpoint/dissect path presence without requiring those paths to exist.
- [ ] `just experiment-smoke` never silently succeeds when required experiment data is missing; messages name the env vars / paths to set.
- [ ] `just bench` has a defined, documented behavior (real harness **or** explicit non-zero “no bench harness yet”).
- [ ] README + agent command docs (`smoke` / `pr-ready`) reference the just surface.
- [ ] No new dependency on multi-GiB weights for `check` / `test` / `build` / `ci` / `doctor`.
- [ ] PR opened from `main` (not from experiment branches); title includes `(#62 / RM-250)`.

## Non-goals (this issue)

* Replacing GitHub Actions with local-only CI.
* Shipping Criterion/kernel GPU benchmarks inside this crate.
* Running full block-0 GOZ1 pilot or τ-sweep as part of default `ci`.
* Codacy / Qodana / Codecov wrappers (optional later; doctor may *mention* them).
* Changing GOZ1 format, quantizer, or manifest semantics.

## Implementation notes

* Branch: start from up-to-date `main`; suggested name `chore/gh-62-unified-check-commands`.
* Prefer one `justfile` over a forest of wrapper scripts; extract `scripts/doctor.sh` only if the doctor logic gets large.
* Keep recipe names stable — agents will hard-code them.
* Estimate: **M** (justfile + docs + wire slash commands; no product-logic changes).

## Related

* GitHub: [https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/issues/62](<https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/issues/62>)
* Agent quality docs: `/smoke`, `/pr-ready`
* Experiment scripts: [RM-221](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-221/grok-ozempic-consume-xai-dissect-run3-planning-surface-pilot-blocks) / [RM-222](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-222/grok-ozempic-gh53-consume-xai-dissect-run3-planning-surface-pilot) (block pilot), [RM-201](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-201/grok-ozempic-research-activity-aware-tier-aware-t-for-spiking-sparse) / [RM-201](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-201/grok-ozempic-research-activity-aware-tier-aware-t-for-spiking-sparse) (τ-sweep)
* Related CLI surface: [#38](<https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/issues/38>) / [RM-193](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-193/grok-ozempic-gh38-cli-for-goz1-run-quantization-token-embedding)

title: [grok-ozempic] GH#32 — Model-agnostic MoE/SNN quantization engine
description:
## Objective

`grok-ozempic` is currently tightly coupled to the Grok-1 model. It contains hard-coded assumptions about:

* Tensor inventory (770 tensors in `grok1_inventory.rs`)
* Tensor naming conventions (V1 `blk.{L}.{role}` and V2 `block_{NNN}.slot_{SS}`)
* Classification rules for routers, norms, MoE experts, attention projections, etc.
* Manifest schema expectations from `xai-dissect`
* Dry-run planning, alignment reporting, and coverage logic that all assume Grok-1 structure

While `magere-brug` provides a higher-level model registry, quantization recipes, and experiment tracking layer, it does **not** provide a reusable quantization engine. The two repos together still only solve the Grok-1 case.

## Goal

Extract a reusable core quantization engine that can support multiple open-source MoE models (Llama-3 MoE, Mixtral, DeepSeek-V2, Qwen2-MoE, etc.) while keeping Grok-1 as the primary/reference implementation.

## Lessons from PR #29 (Testing & Alignment)

PR #29 added 29 new tests for `BackendKernel`, `DryRunPlanner`, and alignment verification. During that work, several pain points emerged that directly inform this generalization effort:

### 1\. Massive test duplication (already partially addressed)

* Every `DryRunPlanner` test repeated the same 3-line setup:

  ```rust
  let m = embedded_grok1_structural_manifest();
  let config = QuantizationConfig::default();
  let report = DryRunPlanner::plan(m, &config).expect("plan should succeed");
  ```
* Extracted `plan_structural_manifest()` helper in `dry_run.rs`, but this is still Grok-1-specific.
* **Generalization impact**: A model-agnostic engine will need a generic test harness or fixture system so adding a new model doesn't require duplicating 10+ test blocks.

### 2\. `.codacy.yml` exclusions reveal structural problems

* Had to exclude `src/**/*` from duplication analysis because test patterns were too repetitive.
* Later narrowed to `src/**/*_test.rs` + `src/**/tests.rs` after CodeRabbit feedback.
* **Generalization impact**: The current test structure will not scale. A generic engine should have model-specific test modules that don't pollute the core test suite.

### 3\. Alignment verification is Grok-1 specific

* `check_alignment()`, `classify_full_inventory()`, `Grok1Inventory::full()` all assume the 770-tensor Grok-1 layout.

### 4\. Structural manifest loading is hardcoded

* `embedded_grok1_structural_manifest()` and `GROK1_STRUCTURAL_MANIFEST_JSON` are compile-time includes.
* V1 vs V2 naming convention handling lives in `manifest.rs` but is still Grok-1 flavored.
* **Generalization impact**: Manifest loading must become model-agnostic with per-model schema plugins.

## Suggested Abstractions

* Introduce a `ModelInventory` trait/plugin instead of the concrete `Grok1Inventory`
* Make tensor name conventions and glob patterns configurable per model
* Allow pluggable classification rules (router, norm, expert, projection, etc.)
* Support multiple manifest schemas (not just xai-dissect V1/V2)
* Per-model default precision tiers and GIF thresholds
* Keep the `BackendKernel` trait and `DryRunPlanner` as model-agnostic

## Non-Goals (keep scope reasonable)

* Do not move CUDA kernels into this repo
* Do not build a full model registry or experiment tracking system (belongs in `magere-brug`)

`magere-brug` would consume the generalized engine. `grok-ozempic` would become one (ideally the reference) implementation of that engine.

* Core types (`BackendKernel`, `DryRunPlanner`, `QuantizationConfig`, etc.) have no Grok-1-specific assumptions
* Grok-1 continues to work with 100% of existing tests passing
* At least one additional model (or a minimal mock inventory) can be added without forking the repo
* Documentation updated to explain how to add support for a new model
* Test duplication is addressed at the architectural level (not just via `.codacy.yml` exclusions)

title: [research] single-scale ternary GOZ1 fails run3 route-preservation gates on block 0
description:
PR [rmems/grok-ozempic#57](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-int8-dequant-export-bounded-block-0-goz1-pilot-53-rm-222-03ffe2525928) produced the first bounded block-0 GOZ1 pilots under the run3 planning surface and measured the route-preservation surface from the packed artifacts. The observed numbers fall well below the run3 gates, and the gap appears to be the information-theoretic ceiling of single-scale ternary rather than a tunable miss.

## Observed route-preservation results (block 0, attention_plus_expert)

| Gate | Threshold | Observed | Status |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| router_top1_agreement | = 99.0 % | 67.77 % | fail |
| router_top2_set_agreement | = 99.5 % | 47.58 % | fail |
| block_output_cosine | = 0.995 | 0.8603 | fail |
| weight_cosine_similarity | *  | 0.8597 | measured |

See reports/grok-1-block-pilot/results.md in PR [rmems/grok-ozempic#57](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-int8-dequant-export-bounded-block-0-goz1-pilot-53-rm-222-03ffe2525928) for full tables and per-projection routing detail.

## Why this is likely a representation ceiling, not bad tau tuning

The best-case least-squares alpha reconstruction of a ternary tensor from {-1, 0, +1} trits can only reach a finite cosine with the original Gaussian-ish weights. For the measured weight distribution the analytic maximum is roughly 0.86-0.90, which matches the observed weight_cosine_similarity and block_output_cosine. Tuning tau changes sparsity but not this asymptotic reconstruction quality for a single shared scale.

## Questions this issue should resolve

1. Is the failure universal across all blocks / modes, or block-0-specific? Issue [#59](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-245/finish-run3-pilot-matrix-blocks-8286063-expert-only-mode) is expanding the matrix to blocks 8/28/60/63 and expert_only.
2. Does per-channel / per-tensor scale (instead of the current single global alpha) materially lift block_output_cosine above 0.995 without re-introducing dense storage?
3. Should the run3 gates be relaxed for the ternary_snn tier, or should attention projections move to a higher-precision tier?
4. Is the synthetic seeded N(0,1) x RMSNorm gain activation distribution too adversarial? A calibration-corpus distribution may shift the numbers, but it is unlikely to close a \~0.14 cosine gap.

## Suggested next steps

* Re-run the route-preservation pipeline with per-channel alpha (scale per leading x last-axis channel) and compare against the single-alpha baseline.
* Document the analytic ternary-reconstruction ceiling in the report so the failure is treated as a scientific result, not a pipeline bug.
* If the matrix in [#59](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-245/finish-run3-pilot-matrix-blocks-8286063-expert-only-mode) shows the same pattern, promote the single-scale ternary conclusion to a project-level constraint for GOZ1 v1.

title: Assign roles to the four block_norm tensors per block (blocks the downstream route-preservation gates)
description:
**Agent:** Claude Code: Fable 5 (xhigh) · found while filling run3's route-preservation surface in grok-ozempic [#53](<https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/issues/53>) / [PR #57](<https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/pull/57>)

## What's missing

`inventory.json` reports **four** `block_norm` tensors per block (slots 7–10) and labels all four identically:

```json
slot  7  [6144]  {"kind": "block_norm"}
slot  8  [6144]  {"kind": "block_norm"}
slot  9  [6144]  {"kind": "block_norm"}
slot 10  [6144]  {"kind": "block_norm"}
```

Their statistics differ substantially, so they are clearly *not* interchangeable — block 0, from `stats.json`:

| slot | rms | peak_to_rms | outlier_fraction |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 7 | 0.734543 | 7.827 | 0.005371 |
| 8 | 0.965007 | 5.462 | 0.006836 |
| 9 | 0.287540 | 8.419 | 0.006348 |
| 10 | 0.536026 | 11.967 | 0.007975 |

Four norms per block implies **sandwich norm** — pre *and* post for both the attention and MoE sub-blocks — i.e. roughly:

```text
h = h + post_attn_norm( attn( pre_attn_norm(h) ) )
h = h + post_moe_norm(  moe(  pre_moe_norm(h)  ) )
```

But which slot is which is not recorded, and the run's `grok_layout_notes` only covers routers.

## Why this blocks the handoff

`grok-ozempic` fills run3's `route-preservation-report.json` gates (`router_top1_agreement ≥ 99.0 %`, `router_top2_set_agreement ≥ 99.5 %`, `block_output_cosine ≥ 0.995`). Doing that correctly requires knowing which norm the router reads, because the router's input is `pre_moe_norm(h + attn_out)` — a *different* norm from the one feeding the attention projection.

Measured on block 0 with the real tensors, the ambiguity is worth **20 points of top-1 agreement**:

| Modelled path | top-1 `slot_04` | top-1 `slot_05` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| projection output straight into router (no residual, no 2nd norm) | 68.63 % | 63.96 % |
| * residual, norms (post=8, pre=9) | 70.24 % | 83.86 % |
| * residual, norms (post=9, pre=8) | **90.65 %** | **95.36 %** |

Under the most favourable assignment at the routing-optimal τ, top-1 reaches **96.97 %** against the 99.0 % gate. Under the other, ~90 %. Same pack, same weights — only the norm role assignment differs.

So the gate outcome (fail) is robust, but **the size of the gap is not reportable** while this is unknown, and the gap size is what decides whether the mechanism needs replacing or just tightening. grok-ozempic currently publishes the no-residual path as an explicit lower bound and documents the ambiguity rather than picking an ordering.

## What would resolve it

Any of these, weakest to strongest:

1. **Record the slot→role mapping** in `inventory.json` / `conversion-manifest.json` as `kind.detail`, the way `moe_expert_projection` already carries `{"projection": "gate"|"up"|"down"}` and `quantized_attention_projection` carries `{"width": …}`. e.g. `{"kind": "block_norm", "detail": {"position": "pre_attn"|"post_attn"|"pre_moe"|"post_moe"}}`.
2. **State the inference and its basis** in `grok_layout_notes` if it can be derived from slot order across all 64 blocks (the ordering does appear stable), even if labelled provisional.
3. **Note it as an explicit unknown** in `route-preservation-report.json` so consumers do not silently pick one — currently nothing signals that the surface has a modelling dependency the producer hasn't pinned down.

(1) is the useful one for the handoff; (3) alone would at least stop a consumer guessing.

## Related, same area

The attention projections are labelled only by width (`narrow` / `model_width`, policy `wrap_existing_int8_unknown`). The shapes actually determine more than that: Grok-1 is grouped-query attention with 48 heads × 128 = 6144 and 8 KV heads × 128 = 1024, so the two `narrow` tensors are **K and V** and the two `model_width` are **Q and the output projection**.

That distinction matters downstream for the same reason: only the output projection's result enters the residual stream the router reads, so of the two `model_width` projections, quantizing one perturbs routing and quantizing the other does not. A `detail: {"role": "q"|"k"|"v"|"o"}` field — even marked provisional — would let consumers stop reporting both and calling it undecidable.

## Non-goals

Not asking xai-dissect to execute inference or compute the gates — the split where it defines the surface and grok-ozempic fills it is right. This is only about recording structural role information the dissect pass is already positioned to determine.

## References

* grok-ozempic report: `reports/grok-1-block-pilot/results.md` § "The routing numbers above are a pessimistic lower bound"
* Consuming issue: rmems/grok-ozempic[#53](<https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/issues/53>) · epic [#48](<https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/issues/48>) · remaining matrix [#59](<https://github.com/rmems/grok-ozempic/issues/59>)
* Run inspected: `grok1_run3_20260802T023050Z`

title: Finish run3 pilot matrix: blocks 8/28/60/63 + expert_only mode
description:
**Agent:** Claude Code: Fable 5 (xhigh) · follow-up to [#53](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-221/grok-ozempic-consume-xai-dissect-run3-planning-surface-pilot-blocks) / [RM-222](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-222) (PR [rmems/grok-ozempic#57](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-int8-dequant-export-bounded-block-0-goz1-pilot-53-rm-222-03ffe2525928))

## Context

[#53](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-221/grok-ozempic-consume-xai-dissect-run3-planning-surface-pilot-blocks) landed the tooling and ran **block 0** in `attention_only` and `attention_plus_expert`. run3's `pilot-selection-plan.json` calls for blocks **0, 8, 28, 60, 63** × modes `attention_only` / `expert_only` / `attention_plus_expert`. This issue is the remaining matrix.

Everything needed is already in place — the driver takes `BLOCK=` / `MODE=`:

```bash
export GROK_OZEMPIC_DISSECT_RUN=~/rmems/xai-dissect/out/LATEST_CORRECT_GROK1_RUN
for b in 8 28 60 63; do
  for m in attention_only expert_only attention_plus_expert; do
    BLOCK=$b MODE=$m scripts/block_pilot_goz1.sh
  done
done
```

## Why this is confirmation, not discovery

[#53](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-221/grok-ozempic-consume-xai-dissect-run3-planning-surface-pilot-blocks) established that the ≥ 0.995 `block_output_cosine` gate is **unreachable with 2-bit ternary at any τ**, with or without per-channel scales — the ceiling (~0.90) is a property of the quantizer, not of a block. So these runs should be scoped as *coverage*, not as a search for a passing configuration.

What they can still tell us, and what makes them worth running:

* **Per-block variation in router sensitivity.** run3 picked 8 and 28 as *near-zero-sensitive router* and 63 as *high peak-to-rms router region*; block 0 was just an early baseline. Whether top-1 agreement varies materially by block is unknown and is the real question here.
* `expert_only` **isolation.** Block 0 never ran expert-only, so the attention vs expert contribution to routing drift has not been separated.
* **Kurtosis spread across blocks.** Block 0's two `model_width` projections differed sharply (8.21 vs 3.42), and the heavier-tailed one sat further below the Gaussian ceiling. Whether late blocks are systematically heavier-tailed feeds directly into per-tier policy.

## Cost

From block-0 measurements: `attention_plus_expert` is ~18.3 GiB of f32 npy staged, ~15 s export, ~33 s pack, ~12.4 GiB peak RSS, ~1.23 GB pack. The npy stage is a `mktemp` dir removed on exit, so only one block's stage exists at a time. Full remaining matrix is 12 runs.

## Acceptance

- [ ] All 4 remaining blocks × 3 modes packed with `--verify`, preserve/ternary counters matching quant-plan intent
- [ ] Route-preservation metrics captured per run
- [ ] Per-block comparison of router top-1/top-2 agreement and projection kurtosis added to `reports/grok-1-block-pilot/`
- [ ] No router or norm ternaryized in any run

title: oz.gif_threshold pack metadata is wrong under per-tensor τ (records defaults||config only)
description:
**Agent:** Claude Code: Fable 5 (xhigh) · found while landing [RM-221](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-221/grok-ozempic-consume-xai-dissect-run3-planning-surface-pilot-blocks) / [RM-222](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-222) (PR [rmems/grok-ozempic#57](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-int8-dequant-export-bounded-block-0-goz1-pilot-53-rm-222-03ffe2525928))

## Problem

`oz.gif_threshold` is written once per pack from the *effective baseline* multiplier, which resolves as `manifest.defaults.gif_threshold || config.gif_threshold`. It therefore **cannot see per-tensor** `ternary_candidates[].gif_threshold`, even though per-tensor τ has the highest precedence in `src/core/precision.rs::resolve_threshold`.

## Demonstrated

The [RM-221](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-221/grok-ozempic-consume-xai-dissect-run3-planning-surface-pilot-blocks) block-0 pilots use a manifest with `defaults.gif_threshold` stripped and per-tensor τ set (attention 0.4, experts 0.9). Both packs record:

```text
oz.gif_threshold = "0.05"      # the CLI default — nothing packed used this value
```

while the measured sparsity proves the real τ applied:

| Tensor | τ actually applied | zeros % | zeros % if τ were 0.05 |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `block_000.slot_04.attn_proj_i8.model_width` | 0.4 | 33.37 | ~4 |
| `block_000.slot_00.moe_expert.gate` | 0.9 | 65.28 | ~4 |

This was flagged as a blind spot in [RM-201](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-201/grok-ozempic-research-activity-aware-tier-aware-t-for-spiking-sparse) / [RM-201](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-201/grok-ozempic-research-activity-aware-tier-aware-t-for-spiking-sparse); [RM-221](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-221/grok-ozempic-consume-xai-dissect-run3-planning-surface-pilot-blocks) is the first run to hit it with a real per-tensor manifest, so it is now a live correctness problem in pack provenance rather than a theoretical one.

## Why it matters

`oz.gif_threshold` is the only in-pack record of quantization strength. A consumer reading `0.05` from a pack whose experts were quantized at `0.9` will mis-model the sparsity regime — and any future audit that trusts the metadata instead of re-measuring trit counts will silently reach the wrong conclusion.

## Suggested fix

Record the τ that actually applied, per tensor, rather than a single pack-level baseline. Options, roughly in order of preference:

1. Add the effective `gif_threshold` to the **per-tensor** entry alongside the existing tier/shape data (needs a GOZ1 header field; container version bump).
2. Keep the pack-level key but write `"mixed"` (or the observed min/max) whenever the resolved per-tensor thresholds are not all equal, so it can never read as a confident wrong number.
3. Minimum viable: leave the value but have `quantize-goz1` **warn** when any per-tensor τ differs from the recorded baseline.

Option 2 is cheap and removes the false-confidence failure mode without a format change; option 1 is the real fix.

## Meanwhile

`.claude/rules/goz1-pipeline.md` now carries the caveat, and `scripts/goz1_trit_histogram.py` (measured sparsity) is the trustworthy evidence path.

## Related

* [RM-201](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-201/grok-ozempic-research-activity-aware-tier-aware-t-for-spiking-sparse) / [RM-201](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-201/grok-ozempic-research-activity-aware-tier-aware-t-for-spiking-sparse) — where the metadata blind spot was first noted
* [RM-221](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-221/grok-ozempic-consume-xai-dissect-run3-planning-surface-pilot-blocks) / [RM-222](https://linear.app/rpd-34/issue/RM-222/grok-ozempic-gh53-consume-xai-dissect-run3-planning-surface-pilot) — first real per-tensor-τ pack; PR [rmems/grok-ozempic#57](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-int8-dequant-export-bounded-block-0-goz1-pilot-53-rm-222-03ffe2525928)

title: card: support language_by_pr override in normalize.language_for
description:
## Problem

`language_for` (`scripts/lib/normalize.py:~772`) returns `card["language"]` unconditionally:

```python
def language_for(card, raw):
    if card.get("language"):
        return str(card["language"])
    # ...extension sniffing only reached when the card omits language
```

There is a per-PR escape hatch for domain (`domain_by_pr`, used by `datasets/cards/limen-axon-encoder-v0.json`) but none for language. A mixed-language repo must therefore either mislabel records or drop `language` from the card entirely, which throws away the curated value for every other PR.

## Concrete case

[rmems/grok-ozempic#42](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-export-grok-1-embedding-pickle-npy-37-rm-189-30ca8c22a3ad) is Python (`scripts/export_grok1_embedding_npy.py`, +620, plus a test file) in a repo whose card declares `"language": "Rust"`. Extracting it today labels a Python trajectory as Rust.

The same applies to the Limen-Neural org, which is Rust + Julia + SystemVerilog across repos and will hit this on any repo with tooling scripts.

## Proposal

Mirror `domain_for`: check `card["language_by_pr"]` (string or int keys, as `domain_by_pr` already tolerates) before falling back to `card["language"]`, then to extension sniffing.

## Acceptance

* `language_by_pr: {"42": "Python"}` overrides the card default for that PR only.
* Existing cards without the field behave identically.
* Test alongside the `domain_by_pr` coverage in `tests/test_collect_and_normalize.py`.

title: normalize: dedupe review_signals and deprioritize 'Addressed in <sha>' acks
description:
## Problem

`extract_review_signals` (`scripts/lib/normalize.py`) can fill all 8 slots with byte-identical text, producing a record with no usable review signal.

Concrete case — [rmems/grok-ozempic#42](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-export-grok-1-embedding-pickle-npy-37-rm-189-30ca8c22a3ad) (`export Grok-1 embedding pickle → .npy`): 51 signals survive the bot filter, but the emitted record is **8 copies of one body**:

> `Addressed in 5ecbe0855124d24533a1cc365274ea2dcb9400c1: portable ~/.models paths in docs/help (no hard-coded username), dtype KeyError guard, NPY header uses space-pad then trailing newline …`

The maintainer posted the same ack across every thread. [rmems/grok-ozempic#43](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-quantize-goz1-cli-for-goz1-run-quantization-38-rm-193-946bde990911) has a milder version (7 unique of 8).

## Cause

Two gaps:

1. **No dedupe.** Nothing compares signal bodies; identical text posted to N threads yields N signals.
2. `_BARE_FIXED_IN_REPLY` **is too narrow** (`normalize.py:~279`). It matches only *bare* `Fixed in <sha>.` / `**Addressed in `abc1234`**`. An ack with trailing content — `Addressed in <sha>: <what changed>` — passes straight through.

Ack-shaped replies are not worthless (they carry the fix rationale), but they are the *answer*, not the *problem statement*. When they crowd out the reviewer comments that prompted them, the trajectory loses its review→patch shape.

## Proposal

* Dedupe on a normalized body key (collapse whitespace, strip the leading `Addressed in <sha>:` / `Fixed in commit <sha>:` prefix) before appending.
* Rank problem statements ahead of acks when the cap forces a choice, so a PR with 6 Codex findings and 20 acks emits the findings.
* Keep at least one ack when it carries rationale — the goal is deduplication, not suppression.

## Acceptance

* [rmems/grok-ozempic#42](https://linear.app/rpd-34/review/feat-export-grok-1-embedding-pickle-npy-37-rm-189-30ca8c22a3ad) emits ≥5 unique bodies.
* Existing `corinth-canal-v0` / `limen-axon-encoder-v0` records do not regress (all currently emit 8 unique).
* Covered by a test in `tests/test_collect_and_normalize.py`.

title: Add SAAQ quantization profile to the benchmark registry
description:
## Goal

Implement the SAAQ (Spiking Adaptive Activity Quantization) quantization profile in the benchmark registry so ternary/SNN-quantized artifacts can be evaluated.

## Context

The benchmark runner registers six quantization profiles: FP16, AWQ, GPTQ, GGUF (all supported), and ternary + SAAQ (registered as hooks but not implemented).

Upstream projects are actively producing SAAQ-quantized artifacts:

* **grok-ozempic**: Ternary quantization of Grok-1 (318GB → \~80GB) using GIF saliency thresholds, GOZ1 binary container format
* **corinth-canal**: SAAQ 1.0 and 1.5 calibration loops across 21 model families

## SAAQ profile specifics

* **Precision tiers**: `preserve` (routing tensors at FP16), `fp16` (passthrough), `ternary_snn` (2-bit {-1, 0, +1})
* **Container format**: GOZ1 (grok-ozempic) or raw ternary-packed tensors
* **GIF threshold**: `tau = gif_threshold * rms` where default `gif_threshold = 0.05`
* **SNN simulation**: Leaky integrate-and-fire membrane model (4 steps, leak=0.9, threshold=1.0)
* **Routing preservation**: MoE gate/router weights must remain at original precision

## Tasks

- [ ] Implement `SAAQQuantizationProfile` in `benchmarks/models.py`
- [ ] Add GOZ1 container format reader (or delegate to grok-ozempic as a library)
- [ ] Add ternary unpacking for {-1, 0, +1} weight matrices
- [ ] Add SAAQ metadata fields to manifest schema (gif_threshold, snn_steps, membrane_leak, formula_version)
- [ ] Add SAAQ-specific metrics: sparsity ratio, ternary coverage, routing tensor preservation check
- [ ] Add sample SAAQ manifest in `configs/manifests/`
- [ ] Add tests for SAAQ profile with synthetic ternary weights

## Acceptance criteria

* SAAQ profile is a first-class quantization method in the registry
* Manifest can describe SAAQ-quantized artifacts with full metadata
* Benchmark runner can dispatch SAAQ artifacts through the evaluation pipeline
* Routing tensor preservation is verified (not quantized)
* Sample manifest passes validation

title: Audit: fix unresolved and resolve bot review items from previous PRs (reply-only fixes)
description:
## Context

Agents have been **resolving PR review threads with reply comments** (`Addressed in <sha>: ...`) **without always landing the corresponding code or doc changes**. GitHub shows the thread as resolved, but the underlying suggestion may still be open in `main`.

This issue tracks a systematic **backfill audit** across merged PRs — not new feature work.

## Problem

Typical failure mode:

1. Bot reviewer (Macroscope, Codacy, Codex, Cursor Bugbot, CodeAnt, etc.) leaves an inline suggestion.
2. Agent replies `Addressed in <commit>…` and marks the thread **Resolved**.
3. The commit either never landed, only partially landed, or the fix regressed after merge.
4. Future agents treat the thread as done because `isResolved == true`.

## Goal

For each targeted merged PR, verify every bot/human inline thread that was marked resolved:

- [ ] The cited commit exists on `main`.
- [ ] The file at the cited line **actually contains** the promised change.
- [ ] Tests / docs still match the bot’s concern.
- [ ] If the fix is missing: implement it, push a follow-up PR, and **re-open** or leave a corrective reply (do not resolve until verified).

## PR audit queue (priority order)

| PR | Title | Why audit |
| -- | -- | -- |
| #37 | handoff-hardening pass | Many Macroscope/Codacy/Codex threads resolved via reply-only pattern in Jul 2026 babysit pass |
| #36 | Grok-1 planning/report surfaces | Large doc + schema surface; Macroscope/CodeAnt reviews |
| #32 | grok-ozempic export contract | Foundational contract; bot threads on schema behavior |
| #20 | Resolve Grok unknown slots and bot followups | Explicit “bot followups” PR — verify none were deferred incorrectly |
| #35 | CI hardening (if merged elsewhere) | Workflow bot comments |

Add others as discovered.

## Workflow (required for agents)

Use the **pr-babysit** discipline, but for **historical** PRs:

```bash
# For each PR number N:
gh pr view N --json mergedAt,mergeCommit,files
gh api graphql … # list reviewThreads where isResolved=true
```

For each resolved thread:

1. Read bot comment + claimed fix commit.
2. `git show <sha> -- <file>` — confirm diff matches claim.
3. `git show main:<file>` — confirm fix still present on current `main`.
4. If missing → implement fix on a branch `audit/pr-<N>-bot-followups`.
5. Reply on the **original PR** (or new PR body) with evidence: file line citation + test command output.
6. Only resolve/re-resolve after **code exists on main**.

### Anti-patterns (do not do)

* ❌ Reply “Addressed in …” without a commit that touches the cited file
* ❌ Resolve thread before CI green on the fix PR
* ❌ Assume `isResolved` means fixed
* ❌ Batch-resolve threads at end of session without per-thread verification

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Audit checklist completed for PRs #37, #36, #32, #20 (minimum).
- [ ] Any gaps filed as sub-tasks or a single follow-up PR with `Fixes #30`.
- [ ] Summary comment on this issue listing: thread count audited, fixes applied, threads left open with rationale.
- [ ] Agent workflow doc note added (optional): link from `docs/` or pr-babysit skill — “resolve only after `git show` verification”.

## Non-goals
